The MRO Buyer manages procurement activities across various departments, ensuring optimal cost-effectiveness, timely delivery, and compliance with quality standards and procurement policies. This role requires effective collaboration with cross-functional teams, internal stakeholders, customers, and external suppliers, as well as a proactive approach to continuous improvement and cost savings.

Primary Responsibilities:

Procurement Planning

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including Engineering and Logistics, to understand procurement requirements, specifications, inventory needs, and priorities. Ensure planning covers MRO materials and office supplies needs.

Order Management

  • Place purchase orders and ensure timely delivery of materials and services, coordinating with suppliers and internal stakeholders to resolve any issues, delays, or supply risks.

Supplier Management

  • Monitor and manage supplier performance, including delivery performance, quality and responsiveness, and compliance with contractual obligations.
  • Conduct regular supplier reviews and evaluations.
  • Seek opportunities for supplier development, improved commercial terms, and long-term supplier relationships.

Record-Keeping

  • Maintain accurate procurement records, including purchase orders, contracts, trackers, and supplier information, according to company policies and procedures.

Inventory Management

  • Collaborate with the planning and relevant internal teams to support adequate inventory levels, considering lead times, operational requirements, and production needs.

Cost Optimization

  • Identify and implement cost-saving measures, sourcing opportunities, and process improvements.
  • Explore opportunities for supplier consolidation, improved commercial terms, and long-term agreements.

Reporting

  • Generate reports and analyses on procurement activities, supplier performance, purchasing performance, and cost-saving initiatives.

Continuous Improvement & Collaboration

  • Proactively identify opportunities to improve procurement processes, lead times, supplier performance, and overall efficiency.
  • Support and participate in Continuous Improvement projects and cross-functional initiatives.
  • Support other procurement categories and team members when needed.

Requirements:

Skills And Competencies

  • Min. 5 years of proven experience as an MRO buyer.
  • In-depth knowledge of procurement processes, best practices, sourcing, negotiation, and supplier management.
  • Proven team player with a collaborative approach and willingness to support others.
  • Strong negotiation, communication, stakeholder management, and problem-solving skills.
  • Proficiency in using procurement software, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and advanced Microsoft Excel.
  • Detail-oriented with strong organizational and time-management skills.
  • Ability to work independently, take ownership, and effectively prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and demanding environment.
  • Proactive mindset with the ability to identify issues, raise risks early, and drive improvements.
  • High-level proficiency in English, including communication with international suppliers and stakeholders.

Experience & Qualification:

  • Bachelorâs degree in mechanical engineering and/or Supply Chain Management.
  • Practical experience in MRO procurement.
  • Proven experience in procurement or supply chain management.
  • Experience in a global or multinational organization is an advantage.
  • Experience in pharmaceutical, automotive, engineering, manufacturing, or import/export industries is an advantage.

company: walkr - turn your Google Meet walk-friendly
description:
Urban Walker

Walkr â London (or another city with strong walkability) Full-time / Part-time considered Â· On-site (outdoors)



About Walkr

Walkr helps people turn everyday calls and meetings into walks. We started as a small Chrome extension that flags walk-friendly meetings in Google Calendar, and we're building toward a bigger mission: make walking the default way people connect, think and work.

We believe most of what happens in a meeting room could happen just as well, if not better, on a pavement. We're now looking for someone to prove it, on the ground, every day.




The role

We're hiring a full-time Urban Walker: someone whose job is to walk. You'll take Walkr's calls, meetings and thinking sessions outdoors, on foot, in a city with enough walkable area to actually make that work. You'll be our internal proof of concept and our most honest source of product feedback.

Practically, this means:

  • Taking scheduled calls and 1:1s while walking, using Walkr to flag and organise them
  • Logging what works and what doesn't: audio quality, routes, weather, pacing, how conversations change when nobody's looking at a screen
  • Feeding that back into the product directly, you'll be in the room (or rather, on the street) with the team building the features you use
  • Scouting and mapping walkable routes near our hubs that others on the team can reuse
  • Occasionally representing Walkr in walking meetings with partners, press or early users



What we're looking for

  • You live in, or are willing to be based in, a city with genuinely walkable areas (parks, canals, low-traffic streets, decent pavements)
  • You're comfortable holding a normal, focused conversation while moving, this is a real skill, not everyone has it
  • You're organised enough to manage a calendar full of outdoor commitments and reroute around weather, meetings and life
  • You're naturally curious about behaviour change, habits and how environment shapes how we think
  • Bonus: you already walk a lot and have opinions about it



Why this role exists

Most companies talk about wellbeing and then put everyone back in a chair in a room with no windows. We'd rather have one person whose entire job disproves the excuse that walking meetings "don't really work in practice." If it's your job, it has to work.


What you'll get

  • A role that pays you to do the thing our product is trying to get everyone else to do
  • Direct input into what we build next
  • Flexible hours built around daylight and your city's best routes
  • The rare chance to put "Professional Walker" on your CV and mean it
